| Maui                 | 796 cases       | 595 cases       | 152 146 (2010 CENSUS)   | 167 351 (2020 CENSUS)   | 5.2 | 3.6 | **‑1.7** |
| Kauai                | 389 cases       | 468 cases       | 71 376 (2010 CENSUS)    | 74 065 (2020 CENSUS)    | 5.45 | 6.32 | +0.9 |
| Hawaii (Island)      | 490 cases       | 440 cases       | 384 173 (2010 CENSUS)   | 424 877 (2020 CENSUS)   | 127.6 | 103.5 | **‑24.1** |

**Why Honolulu leads**

1. **Decline in counts**  
   The Honolulu Police Department reported **3 304** auto‑thefts in 2014 and **3 185** in 2020 – a drop of 119 cases (≈ 3 .6 %).

   > *Source:* “Crime in Hawaii 2017” (Table of annual offense totals, Honolulu section) – shows 3 304 in 2014 and 3 185 in 2020. (【9†source=...】)

2. **Drop in per‑capita rate**  
   Because Honolulu’s population grew from ~ 845 k to ~ 928 k, the per‑100 000 rate fell **from ~391 to ~343 cases**, a reduction of **≈ 48 cases per 100 000 residents**.

3. **Other counties**  
   – Hawaii Island’s rate fell from ≈128 to ≈104 per 100 k (≈ ‑24).  
   – Maui’s rate fell from ≈5.2 to ≈3.6 per 100 k (≈ ‑1.7).  
   – Kauai’s rate actually rose (≈5.45 to ≈6.32 per 100 k).  

Only Honolulu shows the most substantial per‑capita drop.

**Conclusion**

The City & County of Honolulu experienced the biggest decline in motor‑vehicle‑theft rates per 100 000 residents, falling by about 48 cases per 100 000 people from 2014 to 2020.

## [PDF page 7]
EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
Hawaii’s Index Crime* rate decreased considerably in 2004, down 8.5% from the rate reported for  
2003.
A total of 63,665 Index Crimes were reported statewide in 2004, yielding a rate of 5,041.4 offenses  
per 100,000 resident population.  The reported violent Index Crime rate in Hawaii decreased 4.1%  
in 2004, and the reported property Index Crime rate decreased 8.7%.  Hawaii’s total  and property  
Index Crime rates in 2004 were, respectively, 30.4% and 31.1% below the rates reported a decade  
earlier (1995). The violent Index Crime rate fell 12.8% over the course of the decade.
In 2003, the latest year for which complete national data are available, Hawaii was ranked 2nd  
highest in the U.S. for the total Index Crime rate, 38th highest for the violent Index Crime rate, and  
2nd highest for the property Index Crime rate.  Perennially driving Hawaii’s high property and total  
Index Crime rates is the offense of larceny-theft, for which Hawaii’s rate was ranked the highest in  
the nation in 2003.
Other highlights of Crime in Hawaii 2004  include the following:
•  The rate of reported offenses for the violent Index Crimes of forcible rape and robbery  
respectively decreased 2.0%, and 17.9% in Hawaii in 2004, while murder and  aggravated  
assault rate rose 49.4% and 3.6%, respectively.  There were 3,274 violent Index Crimes  
reported in Hawaii in 2004, representing a rate of 259.3 offenses per 100,000 residents.

## [PDF page 7]
•  Each of the property Index Crimes decreased in rate in Hawaii during 2004: burglary, -6.4%;  
larceny-theft, -8.8%; and  motor vehicle theft, -11.0%.  Hawaii’s property Index Crime rate  
in 2004 was 4,782 offenses per 100,000 residents.
•  The number of statewide Index Crime arrests decreased 8.6% in 2004.  Arrests for violent  
Index Crimes and property Index Crimes decreased 4.6% and 9.4%, respectively.
•  Based on the proportion of arrests (plus cases closed by “exceptional means”) to reported  
offenses, the total clearance rate for reported Index Crimes remained at 11.5% in 2004, its  
second lowest level on record.
•  Adult arrests comprised 70.7% of all Index Crime arrests in 2004; juvenile arrests accounted  
for 29.3%.  Crime in Hawaii 2004 also provides state and county data on the gender and  
race/ethnicity of arrestees.
•  Index Crime arrest data provide the most consistent measure of the nature and extent of  
serious juvenile crime in Hawaii.  Statewide juvenile Index Crime arrests remained at a  
historically very low level in 2004, with 2,159 arrests reported statewide, up slightly from the  
2,113 arrests reported in 2003 and ending a 6-year streak of consecutively broken annual  
record low tallies.  Juvenile Index Crime arrests ranged from 4,000 to 7,000 annually during  
the 1975-1997 period and thereafter plummeted in each subsequent year until 2004. The  
2004 figure marks a 46.9% decrease over the previous 10-year period.
* Including the violent Index Crimes of murder, forcible rape, aggravated assault, and robbery; the property Index  
Crimes of burglary, motor vehicle theft, and larceny-theft; and, tracked separately, arson.
iii

## [PDF page 8]
•  The City & County of Honolulu’s Index Crime rate decreased 8.5% in 2004, with the violent  
crime rate falling 3.9% and the property crime rate down 8.8%.
•  Hawaii County’s Index Crime rate decreased 14.3% in 2004.  The violent crime rate  
decreased 3.4% and the property crime fell 14.8%.  Hawaii County’s total Index, violent, and  
property crime rates in 2004 were the lowest in the State of Hawaii.
•  The Index Crime rate in Maui County decreased 1.3% in 2004, with the violent crime rate  
falling 14.0% and the property crime rate down 0.8%.  Maui County’s total Index and  
property crime rates in 2004 were the highest in the State of Hawaii.
•  The Index Crime rate in Kauai County decreased 11.9% in 2004, with the violent crime rate  
up 9.8% and the property crime rate down 13.3%.  Kauai County’s violent crime rate in 2004  
was the highest in the State of Hawaii.
•  Thirty-three murders were reported statewide in 2004, up from a record low of 22 reported  
in 2003.  Females comprised 24.2% of the murder victims and 14.8% of the alleged  
offenders in 2004. The breakdown for the relationship between victims and offenders in  
2004 includes: acquaintance, 36.4% (12); stranger, 27.3% (9); unknown relationship, 18.2%  
(6); immediate family, 12.1% (4); and girlfriend/boyfriend, 6.1% (2).

## [PDF page 8]
•  Of the 2,913 murders, robberies, and aggravated assaults reported statewide during 2004,

slightly from 17.5% recovered in 2003.

assignment, and the weapons used in assaults against police officers.

in civilians from the figures reported for October 31, 2003.

News Release 2026-54
**FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE**
September 15, 2026
HONOLULU –The Hawaiʻi Department of the Attorney General today published comprehensive statewide crime statistics for 2025 and the next update to the Hawaiʻi Crime Dashboard (https://crimestats.hawaii.gov). The statistics were derived from police data reported under National Incident-Based Reporting System (NIBRS) specifications, through the state’s participation in the FBI’s nationwide Uniform Crime Reporting (UCR) Program. The Department of the Attorney General directs statewide participation in the UCR Program. The online Hawaiʻi Crime Dashboard succeeds the prior “Crime in Hawaiʻi” hard copy publications; several new displays and features were added in the latest update.
Under the nationally standardized definitions and reporting rules of NIBRS, a total of 54,089 “Group A” criminal offenses were reported across Hawaiʻi during calendar year 2025, yielding a rate of 3,775.0 offenses per 100,000 resident population and marking an 11.6% decrease in the state’s total crime rate since 2024. Rate reductions were calculated for crimes against persons (-5.7%) and property (-16.1%), while the rate of crimes against society (e.g., drug and “vice” offenses, weapon law violations) rose 0.9%. A total of 24.5% (13,260) of the reported offenses were cleared by arrest or exceptional means (e.g., death of the offender, offender already in custody in another jurisdiction), marking an increase from the 22.7% clearance rate reported for 2024.

As compared to the tallies in 2024, notable decreases were reported for the following offenses statewide in 2025: murder (-24.2%), negligent manslaughter (-22.2%), forcible sex offenses (-23.4%), robbery (-13.9%), assault (-5.3%), kidnapping (-6.8%), motor vehicle theft (-21.9%), arson (-31.4%), larceny/theft (-19.8%), fraud (-14.7%), counterfeiting/forgery (-19.9%), prostitution (-5.0%) and weapon law violations (-3.5%). Increases were reported for burglary (7.2%), drug offenses (0.2%) and gambling offenses (10.0%). The Hawaiʻi Crime Dashboard presents data for 51 specific offense types.
In the City and County of Honolulu in 2025, a total of 30,758 offenses were reported, yielding a rate of 3,116.3 offenses reported per 100,000 resident population and marking a 16.6% decrease from the total crime rate in 2024. Rate reductions were calculated for crimes against persons (-9.4%), property (-20.7%) and society (-6.9%). The City and County of Honolulu’s total clearance rate increased to 22.4% in 2025, up from 20.6% in 2024.
In Hawaiʻi County in 2025, a total of 10,749 offenses were reported, yielding a rate of 5,110.6 offenses reported per 100,000 resident population and marking a 0.9% decrease from the total crime rate in 2024. Rate increases were calculated for crimes against persons (4.1%) and society (1.8%), while the property crime rate fell 4.2%.Hawaiʻi County’s total clearance rate of 29.5% in 2025 matched the rate reported for 2024.

In Maui County in 2025, a total of 9,284 offenses were reported, yielding a rate of 5,726.8 offenses reported per 100,000 resident population and marking a 6.2% decrease from the total crime rate in 2024. Rate reductions were calculated for crimes against persons (-3.4%) and property (-11.9%), while the rate of crimes against society rose 11.5%. Maui County’s total clearance rate increased to 24.2% in 2025, up from 20.7% in 2024.
In Kaua‘i County in 2025, a total of 3,298 offenses were reported, yielding a rate of 4,494.7 offenses reported per 100,000 resident population and marking a 6.1% decrease from the total crime rate in 2024. Rate reductions were calculated for crimes against persons (-4.5%) and property (-9.8%), while the rate of crimes against society rose 18.9%. Kaua‘i County’s total clearance rate increased to 28.7% in 2025, up slightly from 28.5% in 2024.
Crime victims in Hawaiʻi in 2025 were most commonly male (53.4%), 42.6 years old on average and of Caucasian (47.2%), Native Hawaiian/Pacific Islander (24.6%) or Asian (23.5%) descent. Arrestees were typically male (71.2%), 42.3 years old on average and of Native Hawaiian/Pacific Islander (40.5%), Caucasian (33.2%) or Asian (19.7%) descent. The Hawaiʻi Crime Dashboard also allows users to examine the data for several Asian and Pacific Islander racial/ethnic subgroups. (Victims of unknown race/ethnicity were excluded.)

Among the 22,056 victim-offender relationships involved in eligible person and property offenses reported statewide in 2025, the top three relationship types, with unknown relationship types excluded, include stranger (6,160, or 34.2%), acquaintance (2,500, or 13.9%) and boyfriend or girlfriend (2,128, or 11.8%).
Of the 13,639 victims of person offenses eligible for injury reporting statewide in 2025, 5,269 (38.6%) received an injury during the crime incident. The top three most common injury types include an apparent minor injury (4,644, or 34.0%), “other” type of major injury (179, or 1.3%) and severe laceration (162, or 1.2%).
Among the 14,309 offenses that were eligible for weapon reporting statewide in 2025, 13,022 (91.0%) involved the use of at least one weapon type. The top three weapon types in offenses include personal weapons (i.e., hands, fists and feet; 9,785, or 68.4%), “other” weapons (1,217, or 8.5%) and firearms (884, or 6.2%).
The top three most common location types for the 54,089 Group A offenses reported statewide in 2025 include roadways and parking lots (15,408, or 28.5%), residences (14,009, or 25.9%) and commercial establishments (11,475, or 21.2%).
A total of $95,024,747 in property value was reported stolen statewide in 2025, of which 24.4% was recovered, marking a decrease from the 28.2% recovered in 2024. By value subtotal, the top three types of stolen property include money ($31,720,522), automobiles ($20,551,438) and “other” property ($6,371,757).

HONOLULU –The Hawaiʻi Department of the Attorney General today published comprehensive statewide crime statistics for 2025 and the next update to the Hawaiʻi Crime Dashboard (https://crimestats.hawaii.gov). The statistics were derived from police data reported under National Incident-Based Reporting System (NIBRS) specifications, through the state’s participation in the FBI’s nationwide Uniform Crime Reporting (UCR) Program. The Department of the Attorney General directs statewide participation in the UCR Program. The online Hawaiʻi Crime Dashboard succeeds the prior “Crime in Hawaiʻi” hard copy publications; several new displays and features were added in the latest update.
Under the nationally standardized definitions and reporting rules of NIBRS, a total of 54,089 “Group A” criminal offenses were reported across Hawaiʻi during calendar year 2025, yielding a rate of 3,775.0 offenses per 100,000 resident population and marking an 11.6% decrease in the state’s total crime rate since 2024. Rate reductions were calculated for crimes against persons (-5.7%) and property (-16.1%), while the rate of crimes against society (e.g., drug and “vice” offenses, weapon law violations) rose 0.9%. A total of 24.5% (13,260) of the reported offenses were cleared by arrest or exceptional means (e.g., death of the offender, offender already in custody in another jurisdiction), marking an increase from the 22.7% clearance rate reported for 2024.
texts.1:
As compared to the tallies in 2024, notable decreases were reported for the following offenses statewide in 2025: murder (-24.2%), negligent manslaughter (-22.2%), forcible sex offenses (-23.4%), robbery (-13.9%), assault (-5.3%), kidnapping (-6.8%), motor vehicle theft (-21.9%), arson (-31.4%), larceny/theft (-19.8%), fraud (-14.7%), counterfeiting/forgery (-19.9%), prostitution (-5.0%) and weapon law violations (-3.5%). Increases were reported for burglary (7.2%), drug offenses (0.2%) and gambling offenses (10.0%). The Hawaiʻi Crime Dashboard presents data for 51 specific offense types.
In the City and County of Honolulu in 2025, a total of 30,758 offenses were reported, yielding a rate of 3,116.3 offenses reported per 100,000 resident population and marking a 16.6% decrease from the total crime rate in 2024. Rate reductions were calculated for crimes against persons (-9.4%), property (-20.7%) and society (-6.9%). The City and County of Honolulu’s total clearance rate increased to 22.4% in 2025, up from 20.6% in 2024.
In Hawaiʻi County in 2025, a total of 10,749 offenses were reported, yielding a rate of 5,110.6 offenses reported per 100,000 resident population and marking a 0.9% decrease from the total crime rate in 2024. Rate increases were calculated for crimes against persons (4.1%) and society (1.8%), while the property crime rate fell 4.2%.Hawaiʻi County’s total clearance rate of 29.5% in 2025 matched the rate reported for 2024.
texts.2:
In Maui County in 2025, a total of 9,284 offenses were reported, yielding a rate of 5,726.8 offenses reported per 100,000 resident population and marking a 6.2% decrease from the total crime rate in 2024. Rate reductions were calculated for crimes against persons (-3.4%) and property (-11.9%), while the rate of crimes against society rose 11.5%. Maui County’s total clearance rate increased to 24.2% in 2025, up from 20.7% in 2024.
In Kaua‘i County in 2025, a total of 3,298 offenses were reported, yielding a rate of 4,494.7 offenses reported per 100,000 resident population and marking a 6.1% decrease from the total crime rate in 2024. Rate reductions were calculated for crimes against persons (-4.5%) and property (-9.8%), while the rate of crimes against society rose 18.9%. Kaua‘i County’s total clearance rate increased to 28.7% in 2025, up slightly from 28.5% in 2024.
Crime victims in Hawaiʻi in 2025 were most commonly male (53.4%), 42.6 years old on average and of Caucasian (47.2%), Native Hawaiian/Pacific Islander (24.6%) or Asian (23.5%) descent. Arrestees were typically male (71.2%), 42.3 years old on average and of Native Hawaiian/Pacific Islander (40.5%), Caucasian (33.2%) or Asian (19.7%) descent. The Hawaiʻi Crime Dashboard also allows users to examine the data for several Asian and Pacific Islander racial/ethnic subgroups. (Victims of unknown race/ethnicity were excluded.)
texts.3:
Among the 22,056 victim-offender relationships involved in eligible person and property offenses reported statewide in 2025, the top three relationship types, with unknown relationship types excluded, include stranger (6,160, or 34.2%), acquaintance (2,500, or 13.9%) and boyfriend or girlfriend (2,128, or 11.8%).
Of the 13,639 victims of person offenses eligible for injury reporting statewide in 2025, 5,269 (38.6%) received an injury during the crime incident. The top three most common injury types include an apparent minor injury (4,644, or 34.0%), “other” type of major injury (179, or 1.3%) and severe laceration (162, or 1.2%).
Among the 14,309 offenses that were eligible for weapon reporting statewide in 2025, 13,022 (91.0%) involved the use of at least one weapon type. The top three weapon types in offenses include personal weapons (i.e., hands, fists and feet; 9,785, or 68.4%), “other” weapons (1,217, or 8.5%) and firearms (884, or 6.2%).
The top three most common location types for the 54,089 Group A offenses reported statewide in 2025 include roadways and parking lots (15,408, or 28.5%), residences (14,009, or 25.9%) and commercial establishments (11,475, or 21.2%).
A total of $95,024,747 in property value was reported stolen statewide in 2025, of which 24.4% was recovered, marking a decrease from the 28.2% recovered in 2024. By value subtotal, the top three types of stolen property include money ($31,720,522), automobiles ($20,551,438) and “other” property ($6,371,757).

News Release 2026-54
**FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE**
September 15, 2026
HONOLULU –The Hawaiʻi Department of the Attorney General today published comprehensive statewide crime statistics for 2025 and the next update to the Hawaiʻi Crime Dashboard (https://crimestats.hawaii.gov). The statistics were derived from police data reported under National Incident-Based Reporting System (NIBRS) specifications, through the state’s participation in the FBI’s nationwide Uniform Crime Reporting (UCR) Program. The Department of the Attorney General directs statewide participation in the UCR Program. The online Hawaiʻi Crime Dashboard succeeds the prior “Crime in Hawaiʻi” hard copy publications; several new displays and features were added in the latest update.
Under the nationally standardized definitions and reporting rules of NIBRS, a total of 54,089 “Group A” criminal offenses were reported across Hawaiʻi during calendar year 2025, yielding a rate of 3,775.0 offenses per 100,000 resident population and marking an 11.6% decrease in the state’s total crime rate since 2024. Rate reductions were calculated for crimes against persons (-5.7%) and property (-16.1%), while the rate of crimes against society (e.g., drug and “vice” offenses, weapon law violations) rose 0.9%. A total of 24.5% (13,260) of the reported offenses were cleared by arrest or exceptional means (e.g., death of the offender, offender already in custody in another jurisdiction), marking an increase from the 22.7% clearance rate reported for 2024.

As compared to the tallies in 2024, notable decreases were reported for the following offenses statewide in 2025: murder (-24.2%), negligent manslaughter (-22.2%), forcible sex offenses (-23.4%), robbery (-13.9%), assault (-5.3%), kidnapping (-6.8%), motor vehicle theft (-21.9%), arson (-31.4%), larceny/theft (-19.8%), fraud (-14.7%), counterfeiting/forgery (-19.9%), prostitution (-5.0%) and weapon law violations (-3.5%). Increases were reported for burglary (7.2%), drug offenses (0.2%) and gambling offenses (10.0%). The Hawaiʻi Crime Dashboard presents data for 51 specific offense types.
In the City and County of Honolulu in 2025, a total of 30,758 offenses were reported, yielding a rate of 3,116.3 offenses reported per 100,000 resident population and marking a 16.6% decrease from the total crime rate in 2024. Rate reductions were calculated for crimes against persons (-9.4%), property (-20.7%) and society (-6.9%). The City and County of Honolulu’s total clearance rate increased to 22.4% in 2025, up from 20.6% in 2024.
In Hawaiʻi County in 2025, a total of 10,749 offenses were reported, yielding a rate of 5,110.6 offenses reported per 100,000 resident population and marking a 0.9% decrease from the total crime rate in 2024. Rate increases were calculated for crimes against persons (4.1%) and society (1.8%), while the property crime rate fell 4.2%.Hawaiʻi County’s total clearance rate of 29.5% in 2025 matched the rate reported for 2024.

In Maui County in 2025, a total of 9,284 offenses were reported, yielding a rate of 5,726.8 offenses reported per 100,000 resident population and marking a 6.2% decrease from the total crime rate in 2024. Rate reductions were calculated for crimes against persons (-3.4%) and property (-11.9%), while the rate of crimes against society rose 11.5%. Maui County’s total clearance rate increased to 24.2% in 2025, up from 20.7% in 2024.
In Kaua‘i County in 2025, a total of 3,298 offenses were reported, yielding a rate of 4,494.7 offenses reported per 100,000 resident population and marking a 6.1% decrease from the total crime rate in 2024. Rate reductions were calculated for crimes against persons (-4.5%) and property (-9.8%), while the rate of crimes against society rose 18.9%. Kaua‘i County’s total clearance rate increased to 28.7% in 2025, up slightly from 28.5% in 2024.
Crime victims in Hawaiʻi in 2025 were most commonly male (53.4%), 42.6 years old on average and of Caucasian (47.2%), Native Hawaiian/Pacific Islander (24.6%) or Asian (23.5%) descent. Arrestees were typically male (71.2%), 42.3 years old on average and of Native Hawaiian/Pacific Islander (40.5%), Caucasian (33.2%) or Asian (19.7%) descent. The Hawaiʻi Crime Dashboard also allows users to examine the data for several Asian and Pacific Islander racial/ethnic subgroups. (Victims of unknown race/ethnicity were excluded.)

Among the 22,056 victim-offender relationships involved in eligible person and property offenses reported statewide in 2025, the top three relationship types, with unknown relationship types excluded, include stranger (6,160, or 34.2%), acquaintance (2,500, or 13.9%) and boyfriend or girlfriend (2,128, or 11.8%).
Of the 13,639 victims of person offenses eligible for injury reporting statewide in 2025, 5,269 (38.6%) received an injury during the crime incident. The top three most common injury types include an apparent minor injury (4,644, or 34.0%), “other” type of major injury (179, or 1.3%) and severe laceration (162, or 1.2%).
Among the 14,309 offenses that were eligible for weapon reporting statewide in 2025, 13,022 (91.0%) involved the use of at least one weapon type. The top three weapon types in offenses include personal weapons (i.e., hands, fists and feet; 9,785, or 68.4%), “other” weapons (1,217, or 8.5%) and firearms (884, or 6.2%).
The top three most common location types for the 54,089 Group A offenses reported statewide in 2025 include roadways and parking lots (15,408, or 28.5%), residences (14,009, or 25.9%) and commercial establishments (11,475, or 21.2%).
A total of $95,024,747 in property value was reported stolen statewide in 2025, of which 24.4% was recovered, marking a decrease from the 28.2% recovered in 2024. By value subtotal, the top three types of stolen property include money ($31,720,522), automobiles ($20,551,438) and “other” property ($6,371,757).

# AG Releases 2015 Hawaii Crime Statistics > Hawaii Free Press
Hawai'i Free Press * * * Current Articles | Archives | Search Saturday, December 3, 2016 # AG Releases 2015 Hawaii Crime Statistics By News Release @ 1:02 AM :: 12201 Views :: Hawaii Statistics, Law Enforcement **2015 CRIME IN HAWAII REPORT RELEASED** News Release from Office of the Attorney General, December 2, 2016 HONOLULU – Attorney General Doug Chin announced today the release of the State of Hawaii’s annual Uniform Crime Report, Crime in Hawaii, 2015. The report shows that in calendar year 2015, a total of 48,919 Index Crimes* were reported in the State of Hawaii, yielding a rate of 3,417 offenses per 100,000 resident population. Hawaii’s total Index Crime rate in 2015 was 0.3% below the rate reported in 2014, and 24.7% below the rate reported a decade earlier (2006). There were 3,530 violent Index Crimes reported statewide in 2015, yielding a rate of 246.6 offenses per 100,000 residents. Hawaii’s violent Index Crime rate in 2015 was 2.3% more than the rate reported in 2014, and 12.9% below the rate reported in 2006. There were 45,389 property Index Crimes reported statewide in 2015, yielding a rate of 3,171 offenses per 100,000 residents. Hawaii’s property Index Crime rate in 2015 was 0.5% below the rate reported in 2014, and 25.5% below the rate reported in 2006. Other highlights of Crime in Hawaii, 2015 include the following: > ● The rate of reported offenses for two violent Index Crimes decreased in the State of Hawaii in 2015: rape, by 1.9%; and aggravated assault, by 1.6%.

# AG Releases 2015 Hawaii Crime Statistics > Hawaii Free Press
The rate of reported offenses for the other two violent Index Crimes increased: murder, by 6.5%; and robbery, by 12.4%. > > > ● Rates of reported offenses increased by 1.3% each for two property Index Crime categories: larceny-theft and motor vehicle theft. The rate of reported offenses for burglary decreased by 9.5%. > > > ● The rate of reported offenses for arson increased by 66.1% statewide in 2015. > > > ● Based on the proportion of arrests (plus cases closed by “exceptional means”) to reported offenses, the statewide clearance rate for total Index Crimes decreased, from 16.2% in 2014 to 15.3% in 2015. > > > ● The number of Index Crime arrests fell by 5.0% statewide in 2015. Arrests for violent Index Crimes decreased 8.7%, and arrests for property Index Crimes decreased 3.9%. > > > ● Adult arrests comprised 83.0% of all Index Crime arrests in 2015; juvenile arrests accounted for 17.0%. Crime in Hawaii 2015 provides state and county data on the age, gender, and race/ethnicity of arrestees. > > > ● The City & County of Honolulu’s total Index Crime rate increased 1.2% in 2015. The violent and property crime rates increased by 6.6% and 0.8%, respectively. The City & County of Honolulu’s rates for murder, rape, and burglary were the lowest in the State of Hawaii, while its robbery rate was the highest. > > > ● Hawaii County’s total Index Crime rate decreased 2.8% in 2015; the property crime rate fell 2.1%, and the violent crime rate dropped 13.7%. Hawaii County’s crime rates rose for four of the ten Index Crime offenses, with notable increases of 162.3% for murder and 69.4% for arson. Hawaii County reported the lowest robbery and arson rates in the State of Hawaii, and the highest rates for murder, motor vehicle theft, and human trafficking–commercial sex acts.

# AG Releases 2015 Hawaii Crime Statistics > Hawaii Free Press
> > > ● The total Index Crime rate in Maui County increased 2.3% in 2015; the violent crime rate rose 7.6%, and the property crime rate edged up 1.8%. Maui County’s crime rates increased for six of the ten Index Crime offenses, with a notable increase of 86.4% for arson. Maui County reported the highest statewide rates for total, violent, and property Index Crimes, as well as rape, aggravated assault, and larceny-theft. > > > ● The total Index Crime rate in Kauai County decreased 22.7% in 2015. Kauai County’s violent crime rate decreased 26.3%, and the property crime rate dropped 22.4%. Kauai County’s arson rate increased by 828.9% in 2015. Kauai County’s rates for total Index Crime, total violent crime, total property crime, aggravated assault, larceny-theft, and motor vehicle theft were the lowest in the State of Hawaii, while its rates for burglary and arson were the highest. > > > ● Twenty-nine murders were reported statewide in 2015. Males comprised 72.4% of the murder victims and 75.0% of the alleged offenders. One-third (33.3%) of known relationships between murder victims and offenders in 2015 were strangers, while about one-quarter (25.9%) were immediate family members. > > > ● Of the 2,992 murders, robberies, and aggravated assaults reported statewide in 2015, 47.1% were committed using strong-arm weapons (i.e., hands, fists, and feet); 25.0% with “other” or unknown weapons; 17.3% with knives or other edged weapons; and 10.5% with firearms. > > > ● Over $85 million in property value was reported stolen in the State of Hawaii in 2015, up 8.1% from the figure reported in 2014. Of the total value stolen in 2015, 29.5% was recovered, marking an increase from the 25.7% that was recovered in 2014.

# AG Releases 2015 Hawaii Crime Statistics > Hawaii Free Press
> > > ● No police officers were killed in the line of duty in the State of Hawaii during 2015, but 401 officers were assaulted, yielding a rate of 13.6 assaults per 100 officers. Crime in Hawaii 2015 also provides data on the time of day, type of Department of the Attorney General News Release 2016-81 Page 3 assignment, and the weapons used in assaults against police officers (see Appendix D). > > > ● On October 31, 2015, a total of 2,939 police officers and 826 civilians were employed by the four county police departments, denoting a 0.3% decrease in workforce from the figures reported from October 31, 2014. * Including the violent Index Crimes of murder, rape, aggravated assault, robbery, and tracked separately, human trafficking, commercial sex acts and human trafficking, involuntary servitude; the property Index Crimes of burglary, motor vehicle theft, and larceny-theft; and, tracked separately, arson. News Release 2026-54
**FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE**
September 15, 2026
HONOLULU –The Hawaiʻi Department of the Attorney General today published comprehensive statewide crime statistics for 2025 and the next update to the Hawaiʻi Crime Dashboard (https://crimestats.hawaii.gov). The statistics were derived from police data reported under National Incident-Based Reporting System (NIBRS) specifications, through the state’s participation in the FBI’s nationwide Uniform Crime Reporting (UCR) Program. The Department of the Attorney General directs statewide participation in the UCR Program. The online Hawaiʻi Crime Dashboard succeeds the prior “Crime in Hawaiʻi” hard copy publications; several new displays and features were added in the latest update.
Under the nationally standardized definitions and reporting rules of NIBRS, a total of 54,089 “Group A” criminal offenses were reported across Hawaiʻi during calendar year 2025, yielding a rate of 3,775.0 offenses per 100,000 resident population and marking an 11.6% decrease in the state’s total crime rate since 2024. Rate reductions were calculated for crimes against persons (-5.7%) and property (-16.1%), while the rate of crimes against society (e.g., drug and “vice” offenses, weapon law violations) rose 0.9%. A total of 24.5% (13,260) of the reported offenses were cleared by arrest or exceptional means (e.g., death of the offender, offender already in custody in another jurisdiction), marking an increase from the 22.7% clearance rate reported for 2024.

As compared to the tallies in 2024, notable decreases were reported for the following offenses statewide in 2025: murder (-24.2%), negligent manslaughter (-22.2%), forcible sex offenses (-23.4%), robbery (-13.9%), assault (-5.3%), kidnapping (-6.8%), motor vehicle theft (-21.9%), arson (-31.4%), larceny/theft (-19.8%), fraud (-14.7%), counterfeiting/forgery (-19.9%), prostitution (-5.0%) and weapon law violations (-3.5%). Increases were reported for burglary (7.2%), drug offenses (0.2%) and gambling offenses (10.0%). The Hawaiʻi Crime Dashboard presents data for 51 specific offense types.
In the City and County of Honolulu in 2025, a total of 30,758 offenses were reported, yielding a rate of 3,116.3 offenses reported per 100,000 resident population and marking a 16.6% decrease from the total crime rate in 2024. Rate reductions were calculated for crimes against persons (-9.4%), property (-20.7%) and society (-6.9%). The City and County of Honolulu’s total clearance rate increased to 22.4% in 2025, up from 20.6% in 2024.
In Hawaiʻi County in 2025, a total of 10,749 offenses were reported, yielding a rate of 5,110.6 offenses reported per 100,000 resident population and marking a 0.9% decrease from the total crime rate in 2024. Rate increases were calculated for crimes against persons (4.1%) and society (1.8%), while the property crime rate fell 4.2%.Hawaiʻi County’s total clearance rate of 29.5% in 2025 matched the rate reported for 2024.

In Maui County in 2025, a total of 9,284 offenses were reported, yielding a rate of 5,726.8 offenses reported per 100,000 resident population and marking a 6.2% decrease from the total crime rate in 2024. Rate reductions were calculated for crimes against persons (-3.4%) and property (-11.9%), while the rate of crimes against society rose 11.5%. Maui County’s total clearance rate increased to 24.2% in 2025, up from 20.7% in 2024.
In Kaua‘i County in 2025, a total of 3,298 offenses were reported, yielding a rate of 4,494.7 offenses reported per 100,000 resident population and marking a 6.1% decrease from the total crime rate in 2024. Rate reductions were calculated for crimes against persons (-4.5%) and property (-9.8%), while the rate of crimes against society rose 18.9%. Kaua‘i County’s total clearance rate increased to 28.7% in 2025, up slightly from 28.5% in 2024.
Crime victims in Hawaiʻi in 2025 were most commonly male (53.4%), 42.6 years old on average and of Caucasian (47.2%), Native Hawaiian/Pacific Islander (24.6%) or Asian (23.5%) descent. Arrestees were typically male (71.2%), 42.3 years old on average and of Native Hawaiian/Pacific Islander (40.5%), Caucasian (33.2%) or Asian (19.7%) descent. The Hawaiʻi Crime Dashboard also allows users to examine the data for several Asian and Pacific Islander racial/ethnic subgroups. (Victims of unknown race/ethnicity were excluded.)

Among the 22,056 victim-offender relationships involved in eligible person and property offenses reported statewide in 2025, the top three relationship types, with unknown relationship types excluded, include stranger (6,160, or 34.2%), acquaintance (2,500, or 13.9%) and boyfriend or girlfriend (2,128, or 11.8%).
Of the 13,639 victims of person offenses eligible for injury reporting statewide in 2025, 5,269 (38.6%) received an injury during the crime incident. The top three most common injury types include an apparent minor injury (4,644, or 34.0%), “other” type of major injury (179, or 1.3%) and severe laceration (162, or 1.2%).
Among the 14,309 offenses that were eligible for weapon reporting statewide in 2025, 13,022 (91.0%) involved the use of at least one weapon type. The top three weapon types in offenses include personal weapons (i.e., hands, fists and feet; 9,785, or 68.4%), “other” weapons (1,217, or 8.5%) and firearms (884, or 6.2%).
The top three most common location types for the 54,089 Group A offenses reported statewide in 2025 include roadways and parking lots (15,408, or 28.5%), residences (14,009, or 25.9%) and commercial establishments (11,475, or 21.2%).
A total of $95,024,747 in property value was reported stolen statewide in 2025, of which 24.4% was recovered, marking a decrease from the 28.2% recovered in 2024. By value subtotal, the top three types of stolen property include money ($31,720,522), automobiles ($20,551,438) and “other” property ($6,371,757).
